title: AI supporting PRINCE2 Agile
blurb: Say which principle or people aspect an AI use supports, and keep human judgement, communication and data care in place.
question: Larkspur Rail's project manager uses AI to sort hundreds of lessons from past IT projects into searchable, role-specific insights. Which principle does this support, and what must stay with people?

teach.body: PRINCE2 Agile describes how AI can strengthen each principle and the people element: forecasting, finding patterns in lessons, suggesting role assignments, refining plans, drafting stories, testing and sharing information. In every case AI is a support for the project team. It does not remove human decision-making, accountability or the need to talk to stakeholders, and its output is only as good as the data behind it.

head: Principle
How AI can help
rows: Predictive analytics forecasts whether benefits will match timelines and budgets; early warning of overruns
Turns large volumes of lessons into searchable, prioritized, role-specific insights; flags recurring issues and proven fixes
Analyses skills, past performance and workload to suggest role assignments; flags gaps or overlaps
Adjusts time, cost and benefit predictions from progress; refines the next iteration or stage plan
Helps define and decompose products, draft user stories, prioritize backlogs; AI-powered automated testing
Spots similarities with past projects; suggests tailoring and where agile practices fit best

teach.body: AI can help leaders understand the complexity of team relationships, spot individual strengths and track how work is spread across the team. It can automate the collection and sharing of information, give timely insight and handle common questions through a project chatbot. That frees project leaders for strategic, high-impact communication. It does not replace talking with stakeholders.

teach.h: What AI does and what people keep

rows.label: Teams
values: Agree who does what, with the team

head: Practice
AI support drawn from 15.4.1
rows: Forecasting benefits against time and budget
Refining predictions for the next iteration or stage
AI-powered automated testing against quality specifications
teach.caption: A study aid linking the principle examples to the practices they touch.

teach.body: PeopleCert's guidance on AI in PRINCE2 Agile adds practical cautions: treat AI output as a starting point to check, keep authority and accountability with named roles, make sure backlogs, dashboards, risks and lessons are current before relying on AI, and be open about AI use, especially where it processes team feedback or personal data. Record such use in the digital and data management approach.
teach.cite: PeopleCert, How AI can benefit the PRINCE2 Agile professional (white paper, 2026)

teach.h: Worked scenario: Saltmarsh Housing Group's AI assistant
teach.body: The digital team pilots an AI assistant that suggests the likely repair type from a tenant's words and photo. Sally Greaves uses AI to draft user stories for it and to summarize recurring points from retrospectives, which supports focus on products and learning from experience. Contact centre advisers still confirm each diagnosis, the tenants' panel tests the assistant with older tenants and tenants whose first language is not English, and the data use is recorded in the digital and data management approach.

teach.text: Traps: a chatbot answering common questions frees leaders for strategic communication; it does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders. AI forecasting viability is business justification, while AI refining the next stage plan is manage by stages. AI suggests role assignments; it does not decide them.

items: Forecasting viability = continued business justification; mining lessons = learn from experience.
Role suggestions = defined roles; refining next-stage predictions = manage by stages.
Drafting stories and automated testing = focus on products; comparing past projects = tailor.
People: understands team dynamics and workload; automates routine information; chatbot FAQs.
Humans keep decisions, accountability and stakeholder conversations; check data first.

summary: You can now say which principle or people aspect a given AI use supports, from forecasting business justification to drafting user stories. You can also judge whether an AI use keeps human decision-making, stakeholder communication and data care in place.

A.q: Larkspur Rail's project manager, Rhys Pengelly, uses an AI tool to sort several hundred lessons from previous IT projects by topic and make them searchable for each role, highlighting problems that keep recurring. Which principle does this MOST directly support?
A.why: AI supports 'learn from experience' by turning large volumes of lessons into searchable, prioritized, role-specific insights and highlighting recurring issues and proven solutions (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Business justification support is forecasting whether benefits will match timelines and budgets.
whyNot.1: Tailoring support compares past projects to suggest how to adapt the method; here the AI is organizing lessons.
whyNot.3: Focus on products support is defining products, drafting stories and testing.

A.q: Callowmere University's project uses AI to forecast, from historical and current data, whether the hub's expected benefits will still be achieved within the timeline and budget, and to warn early of cost overruns. Which principle does this support?
A.why: AI strengthens continued business justification by forecasting whether anticipated benefits align with projected timelines and budgets and flagging early signs of overruns (15.4.1).

whyNot.1: Manage by stages support refines predictions for the next iteration or stage plan; this is about continued viability.
whyNot.2: Learn from experience support organizes past lessons into insights.
whyNot.3: Roles support analyses skills and workload to suggest role assignments.

A.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's e-commerce team uses AI to break the click and collect feature into smaller products, draft user stories from customer needs, suggest a backlog order, and run AI-powered automated tests. Which principle does this support?
A.why: AI supports 'focus on products' by helping define and decompose products, draft user stories, prioritize backlogs and test against quality specifications (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Tailoring support compares past projects to suggest how to adapt the method.
whyNot.1: Manage by stages support refines predictions for the next iteration or stage.
whyNot.2: Learn from experience support organizes past lessons into insights.

B.q: Draycott Precision Engineering's project manager uses AI to analyse team members' skills, past performance and workload, and it suggests who could take the tester role and flags an overlap in responsibilities. Which principle does this support?
B.why: AI supports defined roles by analysing skills, past performance and workload to suggest role assignments and flag gaps or overlaps (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Tailoring support suggests how to adapt the method from similar past projects.
whyNot.2: Business justification support forecasts benefits against timelines and budgets, not who fits which role.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience support organizes lessons from past projects.

B.q: Easterholm County Council has never run an agile project. Its project manager uses AI to compare Care Online with similar past council projects and suggest how to adapt the method to the project's size and complexity, and where agile practices would fit best. Which principle does this support?
B.why: AI supports 'tailor to suit the project' by identifying similarities with past projects and suggesting how to adapt to size, type and complexity, and where agile practices fit (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience support turns lessons into searchable insights; this output is a tailoring suggestion.
whyNot.1: Focus on products support concerns defining products and stories and testing.
whyNot.3: Business justification support forecasts benefits against timelines and budgets.

B.q: Saltmarsh Housing Group sets up a project chatbot that answers common questions from staff and tenants and sends automated routine updates. According to PRINCE2 Agile, what is the MAIN people benefit?
options: Leaders gain time for strategic communication
Stakeholder meetings are no longer needed
The chatbot decides which groups get which messages
The communication approach can be dropped
B.why: Automating routine information and FAQs lets project leaders focus on strategic, high-impact communication; AI does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders (15.4.2).

whyNot.1: AI supports communication; it does not remove the need to talk with stakeholders.
whyNot.2: Tailoring messages to groups is a human communication decision, supported by AI, not delegated to it.
whyNot.3: The communication management approach still defines how communication and feedback work.

C.q: Larkspur Rail's project manager proposes replacing all briefings with Yusuf Bello's customer relations team by an AI chatbot that answers their questions about the change. Is this an appropriate use of AI in PRINCE2 Agile, and why?
options: Yes, because AI can automate sharing of information
Yes, because a chatbot answers common questions quickly
No, because AI may not be used for the people element
No, because AI does not replace talking to stakeholders
C.why: AI can automate routine information and answer FAQs, but it does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders, especially a worried group facing change (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: AI can automate information sharing, but that does not justify dropping direct conversations.
whyNot.1: Chatbots do answer common questions, but that is a support, not a replacement for briefings.
whyNot.2: The verdict is right but the reason is wrong: PRINCE2 Agile describes AI supporting the people element.

C.q: Draycott Precision Engineering's project manager uses AI to update predictions of time, cost and benefits from sensor-fitting progress, then reviews the refined stage 3 plan with the board at the stage boundary. Is this an appropriate use of AI in PRINCE2 Agile, and why?
options: Yes, because AI approves the next stage plan for the board
Yes, because AI refines the plan and the board decides
No, because predictions are set in initiation and kept
No, because forecasts must use the team's velocity instead
C.why: AI supports 'manage by stages' by adjusting predictions from current progress and refining the next stage plan; the board still makes the decision (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: AI supports the planning; the board, not the AI, approves the next stage plan.
whyNot.2: Plans are updated at each stage boundary, so refreshing predictions is expected.
whyNot.3: Velocity is one input, but AI-refined predictions from progress data are a recognized support.

C.q: Callowmere University's project manager uses AI to analyse workload and relationships in the web team, then lets the tool move user stories between developers without consulting the product owner or the team. Is this an appropriate use of AI in PRINCE2 Agile, and why?
options: Yes, because AI can track how work is spread in a team
Yes, because the PM directs the delivery team members
No, because the people decide, with AI as support
No, because AI must not process data about teams
C.why: AI can help leaders understand team relationships, strengths and workload, but it supports rather than replaces human decision-making; the team and PO decide how work is shared (15.4.2, Table 7.2).

whyNot.0: AI can track workload, but that does not make letting it reassign work appropriate.
whyNot.1: The PO, not the PM, has direct authority over delivery team members.
whyNot.3: PRINCE2 Agile describes AI analysing team relationships and workload; the problem is removing human decisions.

reteach.title: Sat nav on a long drive
reteach.question: Your sat nav predicts arrival times and suggests routes. Who is actually driving?

blocks.body: The sat nav forecasts when you will arrive, learns from past traffic, suggests a faster road and reads out updates so you can concentrate. You still decide whether to take the turn, and you still phone ahead to the people waiting for you. If its map is out of date, its advice is wrong, so you check it.

blocks.h: Sat nav to AI in PRINCE2 Agile
head: Sat nav
AI in PRINCE2 Agile
rows: Refines the next stage plan (manage by stages)

blocks.text: The sat nav does not phone your family for you or choose to skip the trip. AI supports, but people decide and people communicate.

explain.body: For continued business justification, AI forecasts whether benefits will match timelines and budgets. For learn from experience, it turns piles of lessons into searchable, prioritized, role-specific insights.

test.q: Pinewick Home and Garden's AI tool warns that, on current trends, the extra sales from click and collect may fall below what the canvas expects within the fixed budget. Which principle is AI supporting?
test.why: Forecasting whether anticipated benefits align with timelines and budgets supports continued business justification (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Learn from experience support organizes past lessons, not forecasts of benefits.
whyNot.1: Roles support suggests role assignments from skills and workload; this is a warning about viability.
whyNot.3: Focus on products support helps define products and test them.

explain.body: For defined roles, AI suggests role assignments from skills, past performance and workload and flags gaps or overlaps. For manage by stages, it adjusts time, cost and benefit predictions from progress and refines the next iteration or stage plan.

test.q: During stage 2, Saltmarsh Housing Group's AI tool uses progress so far to adjust predictions of cost and benefits and suggests refinements to the stage 3 plan. Which principle does this support?
test.why: AI supports 'manage by stages' by adjusting time, cost and benefit predictions from current progress and refining the next stage plan (15.4.1).

whyNot.0: Roles support suggests role assignments from skills and workload.
whyNot.2: Tailoring support compares past projects to suggest adaptations of the method.
whyNot.3: Learn from experience support organizes past lessons into insight.

explain.body: For focus on products, AI helps define and break down products, draft user stories, prioritize backlogs and run automated tests. For tailor to suit the project, it spots similar past projects and suggests how to adapt the method and where agile practices fit best.

test.q: Easterholm County Council's digital team uses AI to draft user stories for the carers' self-assessment from research notes and to run automated accessibility tests on each form. Which principle does this support?
test.why: Drafting user stories from user needs and AI-powered automated testing support 'focus on products' (15.4.1).

whyNot.1: Tailoring support suggests how to adapt the method, not how to define products.
whyNot.2: Business justification support forecasts benefits against time and budget.
whyNot.3: Roles support suggests who should take which role.

explain.body: AI helps leaders understand team relationships, strengths and workload, automates routine information and answers FAQs through a chatbot. People still decide, stay accountable and communicate directly with stakeholders.

test.q: Callowmere University's project uses AI to send automated weekly progress updates to staff and to answer common questions through a chatbot. Which statement about this is correct?
options: Direct contact with worried staff is no longer needed
The chatbot can replace the communication approach
AI now owns the project's messages to each group
Leaders gain time for strategic, two-way communication
test.why: Automating routine updates and FAQs frees leaders for strategic, high-impact communication, while the need to communicate with stakeholders remains (15.4.2).

whyNot.0: AI does not remove the need to communicate with stakeholders, especially those uneasy about change.
whyNot.1: The communication management approach still defines how communication and feedback work.
whyNot.2: Messaging choices stay with people; AI supports them.
